findings.issue_text: Google Calendar's parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full Zod safeParse result wrapper ({ success: true, data: {...} }) instead of the parsed data, and CalendarService.ts persists this wrapper as the credential key, permanently corrupting Google credentials so all calendar operations and token refreshes fail after the first refresh until the user re-auths (and the fresh credential corrupts again at its next refresh)

createOAuthAppCredential.ts imports throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam from '../oauth/throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam', but the file was never moved into _utils/oauth/ (the old file was never deleted either), so the import path resolves to a nonexistent module and the app-store package fails to build, breaking every OAuth install flow (hubspot, office365video, salesforce, stripepayment, tandemvideo, webex, zoom, zohocrm, zoho-bigin)

refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response object and no call site ever calls .json() on it: Google and Zoho CRM/Bigin crash with TypeError (a Response has no .data), HubSpot silently persists NaN expiry dates, Lark's handleLarkError misparses the sync payload, and Webex's schema parse rejects it, so the sync feature crashes or stores garbage for most apps

Even if the sync response were parsed, the documented contract ('only the access token and expiry date') cannot simultaneously satisfy consumers that read expiry_date (Google), expires_in (HubSpot/O365/Zoom), instance_url (Salesforce), or data.refresh_access_token (Lark)

Salesforce now performs an eager, unconditional token refresh (fetch to login.salesforce.com plus a full credential rewrite) in the constructor on every service construction, adding a round-trip and DB credential write to every operation and failing all Salesforce operations on any transient token-endpoint failure (or a sync deployment without local consumer_key/consumer_secret) even when the cached access token is still valid

The freshly refreshed Salesforce token is only persisted, never passed to the jsforce.Connection constructed immediately after (which still reads the pre-refresh credentialKey), so the eager refresh buys nothing for the current request
Salesforce gates refresh success on response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok, which breaks on any response with an empty reason phrase (HTTP/2/proxies)

Zoho Bigin passes credentialId (credential.id) instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync request body becomes calcomUserId=<credential.id>, causing sync to fail with a 404 or, worse, resolve a different user's tokens and write them to this credential (cross-user credential corruption)

minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys ([z.string().toString()]: z.number()) do not create catch-all patterns — both entries collapse to one fixed literal key — so the schema is effectively 'object with a string access_token' and safeParse silently strips every other field, which callers then persist: O365 overwrites the real refresh token in the DB with the literal string 'refresh_token' (unrecoverable without re-auth if sync is down), Zoom stores a key missing token_type/expires_in, and Salesforce loses instance_url

refreshOAuthTokens never checks response.ok, so 4xx/5xx or HTML error responses from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are treated as success and surface later as misleading TypeErrors or NaN expiry dates at call sites, with no context (status, appSlug, userId) attached, making sync failures undebuggable

Gate mismatch between helpers: refreshOAuthTokens requires userId for the sync path but parseRefreshTokenResponse does not, so team credentials (userId null) on sync deployments are refreshed via the direct provider path but parsed with the stripping/wrapper schema, silently corrupting team-credential keys

Webhook handler app-credential.ts lets malformed payloads produce raw 500s instead of 400s: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse throws an unhandled ZodError and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throws on bad ciphertext or key mismatch
Webhook handler app-credential.ts has no req.method guard, so a GET with no body hits the same code path

Webhook secret is compared with !== (timing-unsafe plain string comparison that short-circuits on the first differing byte), allowing a remote timing attack to recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET byte-by-byte; should use crypto.timingSafeEqual
Webhook check-then-create race: two concurrent webhook calls can both take the create branch and produce duplicate credentials for the same user+app, after which updates hit an arbitrary one
Webhook's findFirst has no orderBy, so it nondeterministically picks an arbitrary credential when duplicates exist

parseRefreshTokenResponse converts previously-handled parse failures at O365 and Zoom into a context-free throw (Error('Invalid refreshed tokens were returned')), discarding the field-level Zod errors and raw provider response that O365 previously logged and that Zoom's caller previously handled gracefully

The outbound sync request in refreshOAuthTokens carries no authentication at all — only calcomUserId and appSlug, with no secret header derived from CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET — so any party who can reach CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT can request live access tokens for arbitrary user ids
No integration test exists per app that exercises a token refresh with sync enabled

parseRefreshTokenResponse's minimum schema is broken: z.string().toString() evaluates to '[object Object]', collapsing both computed keys into one meaningless property so the schema only requires access_token, and since zod strips unknown keys by default, every other token-response field (including expiry_date and the real refresh_token) is stripped; lines 22-24 then write the literal string 'refresh_token' into the parsed data whenever it's missing. Because the schema is selected purely on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT rather than which refresh path actually ran, team-owned Google/Zoom/O365 credentials get their real refresh tokens overwritten with the literal 'refresh_token' and persisted (silent data loss requiring re-auth), Salesforce token responses lose instance_url/signature before being persisted (breaking the jsforce connection), and even in the intended sync path all credentials get a placeholder refresh token, bricking every OAuth credential if sharing is later disabled.

refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in the sync branch, but several callers expect a parsed/axios-style body: Google reads res?.data (a fetch Response has no .data, so token.access_token throws a TypeError), Zoho Bigin and ZohoCRM read tokenInfo.data.error (same TypeError crash), and Hubspot assigns the result to HubspotToken and reads refresh_token/expires_in, yielding undefined fields and NaN expiry so the working credential is overwritten with garbage — the sync feature crashes or corrupts credentials for 4 apps whenever it's enabled.

The outbound token-sync POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication — no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header, signature, or any credential — and the response is trusted wholesale (stored as the user's live credential) with no validation beyond an access_token field existing; anyone who can reach the endpoint can request current access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user IDs (small sequential integers, easy to enumerate), and nothing enforces HTTPS on the endpoint URL.

zoho-bigin passes the credential row ID (credentialId) to refreshOAuthTokens where a user ID is required — the third parameter is documented and used as calcomUserId, and every other app passes credential.userId — so the parent application will look up the wrong user (or none), returning another user's tokens that get persisted onto the wrong Cal.com user's credential (cross-user credential contamination) or simply breaking the sync feature for this app.

The SalesforceCalendarService constructor now refreshes its OAuth token unconditionally on every service instantiation — issuing a token refresh request to login.salesforce.com and a prisma.credential.update with no expiry check (previously jsforce refreshed on demand) — burning Salesforce token-endpoint calls and API limits, adding a DB write per operation (services are constructed per credential per operation), and making every Salesforce calendar operation fail if the token endpoint hiccups or rate-limits, even when credential-sharing is disabled.

The webhook secret guarding apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts is compared with non-constant-time !== and the endpoint has no rate limiting; this secret is the only protection on an endpoint that can overwrite any user's app credentials for any app, so a leaked or brute-forced secret yields full control of all users' OAuth credentials (e.g., swapping a victim's Google/Zoom credential for an attacker's) — use a constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on digests) and rate-limit the route.

The decrypted credential payload in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts is stored with zero schema validation: symmetricDecrypt(...) → JSON.parse(...) → straight into credential.key on both the update and create paths, with no validation that the decrypted JSON matches the shape the target app expects (unlike every other credential write path in the codebase), so a malformed payload from a buggy sender, key mismatch, or anyone holding the shared secret persists garbage that crashes app flows well after the write.

Google Calendar CalendarService.ts:93 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full Zod `safeParse` result (`{ success, data, error }`) instead of the parsed data, so the wrapper object is persisted as `credential.key`; on next instantiation `credential.key.access_token`/`.refresh_token` are undefined (values live under `credential.key.data.*`), breaking every subsequent Google Calendar operation after the first token refresh and re-writing the broken key on each refresh attempt

Salesforce CalendarService.ts:75–97 — the service eagerly and unconditionally POSTs to the Salesforce token endpoint and performs `prisma.credential.update(...)` on every construction of the service with no expiry check, adding a serial network roundtrip (~100–500ms) and a DB write to every Salesforce calendar operation; refresh should be gated on an expiry timestamp or delegated to jsforce's built-in lazy refresh flow

`refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw undici `fetch` Response in sharing mode but provider SDK-shaped results in non-sharing mode; callers written for the provider shape crash or read undefined values — googlecalendar's `res?.data` throws TypeError, zohocrm/zoho-bigin's `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError, and hubspot reads `HubspotToken` fields (`refresh_token`, `expires_in`) as undefined causing NaN expiry and a refresh storm — breaking credential sync for these adapters

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5–10 — broken computed-key Zod schema: `z.string().toString()` evaluates to `"[object Object]"` so both computed keys collide and the second overwrites the first; the schema only enforces `access_token` and silently strips all other fields (`expiry_date`, `refresh_token`, `instance_url`, etc.), after which the `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` mutation persists a literal placeholder into credentials, destroying real refresh tokens for O365/Zoom (Zoom tokens are single-use)

Zoho Bigin CalendarService.ts:90 — passes `credentialId` as the `userId` argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` (every other adapter passes `credential.userId`), causing the sync endpoint to look up or write credentials against the wrong entity in the parent application

Office365 CalendarService.ts:252 in sharing mode — the minimum schema strips `expiry_date` from the sync response, so merged credentials retain the old (always past) expiry timestamp, causing a token refresh plus `prisma.credential.update` on every calendar operation (network and write amplification across all O365 bookings)

No timeout/`AbortSignal` on the credential-sync `fetch()` in refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10–16 or the new Salesforce fetch in salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — a slow or hung sync endpoint stalls the booking critical path (availability checks and booking creation hold request workers/concurrency slots for minutes)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:28 — `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws an unhandled ZodError on malformed/missing bodies (e.g., a GET with no body), producing 500s instead of 400s; should use `safeParse` and there is no HTTP method guard to reject non-POST requests

Google Calendar credentials are corrupted for all deployments: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:31) returns the whole Zod `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper (`{ success, data, error }`) instead of `.data`, and googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 assigns it directly to the persisted credential key, so on the first routine token refresh the stored credential shape breaks auth and refresh permanently (until manual re-auth) and the schema-validation guarantee before DB write is lost; not gated by the new env flags

`refreshOAuthTokens` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:16-18) returns a raw fetch `Response` in sync mode, incompatible with every consuming adapter: Google reads `res?.data` (undefined → TypeError on `token.access_token`), Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin expect axios responses (`tokenInfo.data.error` throws on undefined), Hubspot expects a `HubspotToken` object (undefined fields → NaN expiry persisted), Lark feeds it to `handleLarkError` which expects the `{code, msg, data}` envelope, and zoom/webex/o365/msteams parse provider-specific key names (`expires_in`, `expiry_date`) that the documented sync response never defines — the credential-sync feature cannot work against its own documented contract and several adapters hard-crash

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:27-29) stores the literal string "refresh_token" as the refresh token whenever the parsed response lacks one, which is always true in sync mode; Office365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~258) spreads `tokenResponse.data` over existing credentials, overwriting a valid refresh token with the literal string so the next refresh sends garbage to Microsoft/Zoom → `invalid_grant` → credential permanently bricked; same poisoning applies to Zoom's stored key

The outbound credential-sync POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11-17) sends only `calcomUserId` + `appSlug` with no authentication or secret header; `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is only used on the inbound webhook, so the parent app cannot verify the caller and anyone who learns the URL can request live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs/app slugs

Salesforce (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~86) checks `response.statusText !== "OK"`, but over HTTP/2 (negotiated via ALPN on login.salesforce.com) fetch responses carry no reason phrase so `statusText` is `""` even on 200, throwing `HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: "" })` on successful responses; should check `response.ok`

`minimumTokenResponseSchema` (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-10) uses `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` as computed keys, both of which evaluate to the key "[object Object]" (Zod schemas don't override toString; the second duplicate key wins), so the intended 'any numeric property is the expiry' contract is not implemented and `z.object` strips expiry fields from `data`, leaving downstream expiry math (`expiry_date`, `expires_in`) with `undefined` → NaN expiry persisted in sync mode

Salesforce token refresh now runs unconditionally on every service construction (salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99) with no expiry check (previously jsforce refreshed on demand), adding an extra HTTP round-trip and `prisma.credential.update` DB write per booking/availability call, exposing Salesforce rate limits and creating concurrent-write races on the credential row

O365 refresh failures now throw instead of degrading: the removed `if (!tokenResponse.success) console.error(...)` block (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~246-260) meant malformed MS responses were logged and the flow continued with existing credentials, but `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws instead, so a transient bad MS response now aborts the operation up the booking stack instead of being best-effort

Zoho Bigin (zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:~91) passes `credentialId` to `refreshOAuthTokens` where every other adapter passes `credential.userId`, so the outbound payload carries `calcomUserId: <credentialId>`, violating the payload contract the parent app implements against and causing it to map to the wrong or nonexistent user → sync fails or returns the wrong account's tokens

Unhandled ZodError / `symmetricDecrypt` / `JSON.parse` failures in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts (lines 34, 62-64) produce 500 responses where integrators need 4xx to distinguish their own bad payloads (wrong body shape, mismatched encryption key) from server faults
The webhook endpoint app-credential.ts has no `req.method` check (line 16), so any HTTP verb including GET mutates credential state
The webhook auth secret is compared with `!==` (app-credential.ts:22-26), a timing side channel; it should use `timingSafeEqual`

`req.headers[headerName]` in app-credential.ts requires `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` to be lowercase (Node lowercases header names), so a mixed-case env value fails closed for all callers — a silent footgun at the auth boundary

(Verify) zoho-bigin (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17) hardcodes the redirect URI `WEBAPP_URL + '/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback'` replacing the `appConfig.slug`-derived value; redirect URIs are externally registered with Zoho and must match byte-for-byte, so confirm the slug equals "zoho-bigin" and that `callback.ts`'s token exchange uses the identical value

(Verify) Salesforce CalendarService adds usages of `prisma` (~line 96, `prisma.credential.update`) and `HttpError` (~line 86) with no imports added in the diff; if they don't pre-exist, this is a build/runtime break

parseRefreshTokenResponse (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29) returns the zod safeParse wrapper ({ success: true, data: {...} }) instead of the parsed data, and GoogleCalendarService (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:96-99) persists this wrapper directly as the credential key, so the next schema parse fails and every Google-connected user's calendar breaks at the first routine token refresh (staying broken until manual DB repair).

refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15) returns a raw fetch Response when sync is enabled but provider-specific objects from the local fallback, breaking consumers that read provider-specific shapes: googlecalendar (CalendarService.ts:93-94) reads res?.data which is undefined on a Response causing a TypeError on token.access_token; hubspot (CalendarService.ts:176-189) expects a parsed HubspotToken so expires_in/refresh_token are undefined, persisting a NaN expiryDate and losing the refresh token; zoho-bigin (CalendarService.ts:85-96) and zohocrm (CalendarService.ts:204-217) throw TypeError accessing .data on a Response.

The generic 'access token + expiry' sync payload doesn't match the provider-specific parsers of the fetch-based consumers either (Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope; Zoom/O365/MS-Teams schemas requiring refresh_token/expires_in), so even the consistent call sites fail to parse it.

parseRefreshTokenResponse (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27) injects a literal 'refresh_token' placeholder string when the field is missing, and it is persisted over the user's real refresh token in the DB (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 and zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:104), irrecoverably destroying the credential — later local refresh sends the string 'refresh_token' to the provider and the integration is permanently dead.

minimumTokenResponseSchema (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8,10) uses z.string().toString() which evaluates to '[object Object]', so the object literal has keys access_token and '[object Object]'; because zod's z.object strips unknown keys by default, the parsed data retains only access_token — no numeric expiry, expires_in, expiry_date, or instance_url. Office365's expiry is never updated (sync refresh fires on every calendar operation), Zoom computes expiryDate as NaN, and Salesforce's stored key loses instance_url, id, issued_at, etc.

The sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14) has no AbortSignal/timeout, so a hung sync endpoint stalls bookings indefinitely since token refresh happens in the booking hot path.

The sync fetch does not check response.ok (fetch doesn't throw on 4xx/5xx), so an endpoint-down 500 flows into the token parsers as 'Invalid refreshed tokens' with no distinction between an outage and a bad payload.
The sync fetch has no retry/backoff and no fallback to the local refreshFunction (which still holds a valid refresh token), so a single sync-endpoint blip fails bookings that would otherwise succeed.

The outbound sync request (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14) is unauthenticated — it sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET header even though the inbound webhook (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29) is gated on that secret — so any party that can reach the sync endpoint can mint/fetch live OAuth access tokens for any user.

The Salesforce constructor path (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:74-99) now always POSTs to the token endpoint and writes to the DB on every service instantiation with no expiry check (previously jsforce refreshed lazily only on 401), no try/catch, and no timeout — a transient network/5xx error from the token endpoint fails every Salesforce calendar operation even when the cached token was still valid, and every booking adds a full token-refresh round trip plus a DB write (latency, rate-limit exposure, thundering herd).

Salesforce success check uses response.statusText !== 'OK' (salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86) instead of response.ok — the HTTP reason phrase is optional per RFC 7230 and empty on HTTP/2 connections and some proxies, so a successful 200 is misclassified as a failure and throws HttpError 400.

zoho-bigin (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85-93) passes credentialId — the credential's primary key — where every other call site passes credential.userId, so refreshOAuthTokens sends the wrong id as calcomUserId: sync fails, or worse, the webhook handler (app-credential.ts:34,62-65) matches some other user's id and writes this user's tokens onto another user's credential.
The webhook handler (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31) has no req.method guard, so a GET with no body still hits the request body schema.

The webhook handler (app-credential.ts:57-59) lets appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throw uncaught on malformed/undecryptable input, producing generic 500s — a caller can't distinguish a permanent 4xx (don't retry) from a transient 5xx (retry), so a bad payload can be retried forever; should use safeParse with explicit 400s.

The webhook handler's findFirst-then-update/create flow (app-credential.ts:62-88) has no transaction and there is no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent sync deliveries for the same user+app both take the create branch and produce duplicate credential rows, making later credential selection ambiguous for that app.

parseRefreshTokenResponse has two conflicting return contracts: it returns the full safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), but the Google call site (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~95) treats it as the parsed value and persists the Zod envelope as the credential key via prisma.credential.update — every token refresh overwrites the stored Google credential with { success: true, data: ... }, so the next instantiation/refresh fails; silent OAuth-token data loss for all deployments, not just credential-sync users.

refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-17) is typed as returning any and leaks two incompatible shapes — a raw fetch Response on the sync path vs provider-native objects (gaxios, axios, hubspot SDK) on the native path — so sync mode is structurally broken for most providers: Google reads res?.data (undefined on a Response) and throws TypeError, zoho-bigin/zohocrm use axios-shaped .data.error on a Response, Hubspot persists a Response as a HubspotToken, Lark feeds a sync Response to handleLarkError which requires {code, msg, data}, and Webex expects its {message} error shape; the helper should normalize (await + parse the token JSON, return tokens).

minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:4-9) both evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' because zod schemas don't override toString — the duplicate key lets z.unknown().optional() silently replace the intended expiry validation, the schema's comments describe behavior that does not exist, and the non-literal computed keys degrade the TS type to an index signature, erasing type safety for every caller.

z.object strips unknown keys by default, so data parsed by minimumTokenResponseSchema contains only access_token (plus the injected placeholder): in sync mode expiry_date/expires_in is never persisted, causing Office365/Zoom to re-refresh on every operation, and Salesforce (CalendarService.ts:~91) — which uses this schema whenever the feature flag is on even though its fetch goes directly to login.salesforce.com — has instance_url, signature and issued_at stripped from the stored credential, breaking the next jsforce.Connection.

Guard mismatch between refreshOAuthTokens (takes the sync path only when userId is truthy) and parseRefreshTokenResponse (applies the stripping minimum schema whenever flag+endpoint are set, with no userId check): for team-owned credentials (userId null) the refresh runs natively and returns real tokens, but the response is parsed with the minimum schema — everything but access_token is stripped and data.refresh_token is set to the literal 'refresh_token' — then spread over and persisted to the real credential (e.g. Office365 CalendarService.ts:~250), destroying the just-obtained real refresh token so the next refresh fails.
The 'refresh_token' magic placeholder is a one-way door: any later disabling of the sync endpoint bricks every synced credential with no migration path.

zoho-bigin (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:~93) passes credentialId as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens where the user id is expected (it's sent as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint), so in sync mode the parent app maps tokens to the wrong user; every sibling service correctly passes credential.userId.

The outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:9-15) is unauthenticated — it sends only calcomUserId + appSlug with no auth header, an inconsistent trust model given the inbound webhook requires a shared secret — and it has no timeout and its response status is never checked, so a 4xx/5xx/HTML error page is passed downstream as if it were a token payload.

The credential-sync request payload ('Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires') is hardcoded inside shared library code rather than in config, so the intended customization point lives in a file every consumer shares.

Salesforce (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-95) now performs an unconditional network refresh plus credential DB write in the constructor's async flow on every service instantiation with no expiry check (previously refresh was deferred to jsforce), and it bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely — inconsistent with the pattern applied to 9 sibling services — so in sync mode the stored refresh_token is the 'refresh_token' placeholder and the direct fetch to login.salesforce.com fails on every operation.
Salesforce uses a fragile success check, response.statusText !== 'OK', instead of response.ok.

The webhook upsert (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58-88) is a non-atomic check-then-act: findFirst with no orderBy followed by update/create lets concurrent webhooks create duplicate (userId, appId) credentials and update an arbitrary row when duplicates already exist; the comment claiming prisma upsert can't be used is incorrect (upsert accepts any unique-constraint where), and a transaction or unique constraint would make it atomic.

The webhook handler (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:14-31) accepts any HTTP method — a GET with no body hits appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and throws unhandled — and symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse failures are also unhandled, so malformed or hostile input produces 500s instead of 400/401 on an unauthenticated-surface-adjacent endpoint.

The decrypted credential payload is persisted (app-credential.ts:44-50) without validating it against the target app's zod schema (googleCredentialSchema, O365AuthCredentials, etc.), so parent-app payload drift surfaces as TypeErrors deep inside booking flows instead of being caught at the boundary.

zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 hardcodes the literal 'zoho-bigin' in the redirect URI, replacing appConfig.slug while callback.ts in the same app still uses it — duplicating the constant (drift/rename hazard) with a change unrelated to the PR's purpose.
The hardcoded app slug strings passed to refreshOAuthTokens across 9 services ('google-calendar', 'msteams', ...) have no shared constant tying them to each app's config.json.
Dead code: salesforce CalendarService.ts:~90's if (!accessTokenParsed.success) check is unreachable because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on failure.
Dead code: refreshOAuthTokens.ts:19-21's else branch (const response = await refreshFunction(); return response;) adds nothing.

Dead code: app-credential.ts:46's process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || '' — the flag gate guarantees the key is set, so the '' fallback is dead, and if it were ever live it would decrypt with an empty key instead of failing.

The sync-on/off predicate is expressed as two different raw process.env expressions in three files (refreshOAuthTokens, parseRefreshTokenResponse, the webhook) while the flag itself lives in @calcom/lib/constants — centralizing endpoint/header/secret/key access there would have prevented the drift between the two helpers' guards.

Google Calendar credential is corrupted by the safeParse envelope: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~96-99) returns the Zod `{ success, data, error }` envelope which is stored directly as `credential.key` instead of the parsed data, so after the first token refresh every subsequent refresh and calendar operation fails until the user manually re-auths — data loss on the default path for all Google Calendar integrations

The minimum token schema (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11) is a silent-pass guard: `[z.string().toString()]` produces the literal key `"[object Object]"` so the effective schema is only `{ access_token: string }`, and z.object strips unknown keys — silently discarding `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, and expiry fields, while bypassing the real provider schemas (zoom, O365, Salesforce) entirely when sync is enabled, so any garbage response with an `access_token` string validates green

Fabricated `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` literal string overwrites the user's real refresh token: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-29 injects the literal when parsed data lacks `refresh_token` and callers persist it — the O365 merge (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~252-254) spreads the fabricated value last over stored credentials, permanently destroying the real refresh token so the credential can never be refreshed again

Sync mode returns a raw `fetch` Response where callers expect a provider-shaped token object (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16): Google's `res?.data` throws TypeError since Response has no `.data`, Hubspot reads `refresh_token`/`expires_in` off the Response and persists `undefined`/`NaN` into the credential, and Zoho's `tokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError — every adapter breaks the moment the sync path is taken

The outbound token sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication at all (no secret, signature, or credential) despite the endpoint handing back live OAuth access tokens for a caller-supplied `calcomUserId`, and userIds are small sequential integers trivially enumerable — anyone who can reach the endpoint can steal access tokens for arbitrary users

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8,10) uses z.string().toString() which evaluates to '[object Object]', so the object literal has keys access_token and '[object Object]'; because zod's z.object strips unknown keys by default, the parsed data retains only access_token — no numeric expiry, expires_in, expiry_date, or instance_url. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These are evaluated immediately as plain JS property names; `z.string()` is an object, so `.toString()` will not create a dynamic “any string key” and instead produces a single literal key (and both computed keys collide). As a result, when the “minimum” schema is used (when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set), Zod will strip real token fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, `instance_url`, etc., leaving essentially only `access_token` (plus the artificially injected `refresh_token`). adjudication_records.issue_text: The sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14) has no AbortSignal/timeout, so a hung sync endpoint stalls bookings indefinitely since token refresh happens in the booking hot path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, it does a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` with no `AbortSignal`/timeout. adjudication_records.issue_text: The sync fetch does not check response.ok (fetch doesn't throw on 4xx/5xx), so an endpoint-down 500 flows into the token parsers as 'Invalid refreshed tokens' with no distinction between an outage and a bad payload.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync path does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and immediately returns the `Response` without checking `response.ok` or otherwise handling non-2xx statuses. adjudication_records.issue_text: The Salesforce constructor path (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:74-99) now always POSTs to the token endpoint and writes to the DB on every service instantiation with no expiry check (previously jsforce refreshed lazily only on 401), no try/catch, and no timeout — a transient network/5xx error from the token endpoint fails every Salesforce calendar operation even when the cached token was still valid, and every booking adds a full token-refresh round trip plus a DB write (latency, rate-limit exposure, thundering herd).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the constructor now unconditionally calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then immediately `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection`. While this is a concrete resilience/performance regression grounded in the diff (extra round-trip + DB write per instantiation), whether it’s a "bug" depends on intended lifecycle/instantiation frequency and token validity expectations, which aren’t shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce success check uses response.statusText !== 'OK' (salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86) instead of response.ok — the HTTP reason phrase is optional per RFC 7230 and empty on HTTP/2 connections and some proxies, so a successful 200 is misclassified as a failure and throws HttpError 400.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh-token fetch checks success via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`. `statusText` is not a reliable indicator of HTTP success (it can be empty or vary), so a successful 2xx response could incorrectly throw, whereas `response.ok`/`response.status` should be used. adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85-93) passes credentialId — the credential's primary key — where every other call site passes credential.userId, so refreshOAuthTokens sends the wrong id as calcomUserId: sync fails, or worse, the webhook handler (app-credential.ts:34,62-65) matches some other user's id and writes this user's tokens onto another user's credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook handler (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31) has no req.method guard, so a GET with no body still hits the request body schema.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook handler (app-credential.ts:57-59) lets appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throw uncaught on malformed/undecryptable input, producing generic 500s — a caller can't distinguish a permanent 4xx (don't retry) from a transient 5xx (retry), so a bad payload can be retried forever; should use safeParse with explicit 400s.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and then `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without any try/catch or `safeParse` handling. This makes malformed/undecryptable payloads look like server errors instead of explicit 4xx client errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook handler's findFirst-then-update/create flow (app-credential.ts:62-88) has no transaction and there is no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent sync deliveries for the same user+app both take the create branch and produce duplicate credential rows, making later credential selection ambiguous for that app.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse has two conflicting return contracts: it returns the full safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), but the Google call site (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~95) treats it as the parsed value and persists the Zod envelope as the credential key via prisma.credential.update — every token refresh overwrites the stored Google credential with { success: true, data: ... }, so the next instantiation/refresh fails; silent OAuth-token data loss for all deployments, not just credential-sync users.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data`. However, in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the call site assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This would store the Zod envelope (e.g., `{ success: true, data: ... }`) as the credential `key`, corrupting the stored credential shape and likely breaking subsequent uses that expect the raw credential fields (access_token, refresh_token, expiry_date, etc.). adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-17) is typed as returning any and leaks two incompatible shapes — a raw fetch Response on the sync path vs provider-native objects (gaxios, axios, hubspot SDK) on the native path — so sync mode is structurally broken for most providers: Google reads res?.data (undefined on a Response) and throws TypeError, zoho-bigin/zohocrm use axios-shaped .data.error on a Response, Hubspot persists a Response as a HubspotToken, Lark feeds a sync Response to handleLarkError which requires {code, msg, data}, and Webex expects its {message} error shape; the helper should normalize (await + parse the token JSON, return tokens).

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: refreshOAuthTokens() returns the raw fetch Response when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-17). Multiple call sites then treat the returned value as a provider-specific token object/HTTP client response, which will break in sync mode. For example, GoogleCalendarService does `const token = res?.data;` after calling refreshOAuthTokens (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), but a fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token` becomes undefined and `token.access_token` will throw. Similarly, zoho-bigin and zohocrm CalendarService access `tokenInfo.data` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` after calling refreshOAuthTokens (axios shape), which will be undefined on a fetch Response. This mismatch is introduced by the diff and is a real correctness defect unless all sync endpoints return exactly the same shape and callers are updated to parse JSON.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:4-9) both evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' because zod schemas don't override toString — the duplicate key lets z.unknown().optional() silently replace the intended expiry validation, the schema's comments describe behavior that does not exist, and the non-literal computed keys degrade the TS type to an index signature, erasing type safety for every caller.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to model “any numeric property is expiry” and “allow other properties” using computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. In JS object literals these computed keys become a single literal property name (derived from the Zod object’s `toString()`), not a dynamic/index signature, and the second entry overwrites the first if they resolve to the same string. As a result, the schema does not actually validate arbitrary numeric expiry fields as the comments claim, and instead effectively degrades to (at best) one fixed extra property definition. This is a concrete correctness issue in the new schema used when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is on.

adjudication_records.issue_text: z.object strips unknown keys by default, so data parsed by minimumTokenResponseSchema contains only access_token (plus the injected placeholder): in sync mode expiry_date/expires_in is never persisted, causing Office365/Zoom to re-refresh on every operation, and Salesforce (CalendarService.ts:~91) — which uses this schema whenever the feature flag is on even though its fetch goes directly to login.salesforce.com — has instance_url, signature and issued_at stripped from the stored credential, breaking the next jsforce.Connection.

adjudication.rationale: In `_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, the code unconditionally parses token refresh responses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the app-specific schema. That schema is a `z.object(...)` without `.passthrough()`/`.catchall()`, so even if it succeeds it will not preserve extra fields (e.g., `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, Salesforce `instance_url/signature/issued_at`) in `refreshTokenResponse.data`. This parsed `data` is then merged/persisted (e.g., Office365 `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.data) }`, Zoom uses the parsed result, Salesforce persists `{ ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: ... }`), so required fields can be lost in “sync mode,” breaking behavior. Additionally, the computed-key attempt (`[z.string().toString()]`) does not implement a true index signature, making the minimal schema unreliable for real responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guard mismatch between refreshOAuthTokens (takes the sync path only when userId is truthy) and parseRefreshTokenResponse (applies the stripping minimum schema whenever flag+endpoint are set, with no userId check): for team-owned credentials (userId null) the refresh runs natively and returns real tokens, but the response is parsed with the minimum schema — everything but access_token is stripped and data.refresh_token is set to the literal 'refresh_token' — then spread over and persisted to the real credential (e.g. Office365 CalendarService.ts:~250), destroying the just-obtained real refresh token so the next refresh fails.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a real guard mismatch. `refreshOAuthTokens` only uses the credential-sync endpoint when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (so team-owned creds with `userId` null take the native refresh path). But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to `minimumTokenResponseSchema` whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (no `userId` check), so the native provider refresh responses for team creds will be parsed with the “minimum” schema. That schema is not `.passthrough()`, so it will drop unknown fields like `refresh_token`/expiry fields, then the helper forcibly sets `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. In Office365 (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), the parsed data is spread into `o365AuthCredentials` and persisted via `prisma.credential.update`, which would overwrite the real refresh token with the literal string, breaking subsequent refreshes (data loss).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'refresh_token' magic placeholder is a one-way door: any later disabling of the sync endpoint bricks every synced credential with no migration path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, which—when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set—validates only a minimal token shape and then forcibly sets a missing `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:~93) passes credentialId as the third argument to refreshOAuthTokens where the user id is expected (it's sent as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint), so in sync mode the parent app maps tokens to the wrong user; every sibling service correctly passes credential.userId.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument. But `refreshOAuthTokens` is defined as `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)` and, in sync mode, sends it as `calcomUserId` (`userId.toString()`) to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. adjudication_records.issue_text: The outbound POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:9-15) is unauthenticated — it sends only calcomUserId + appSlug with no auth header, an inconsistent trust model given the inbound webhook requires a shared secret — and it has no timeout and its response status is never checked, so a 4xx/5xx/HTML error page is passed downstream as if it were a token payload.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no authentication headers and no timeout/abort signal. adjudication_records.issue_text: The credential-sync request payload ('Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires') is hardcoded inside shared library code rather than in config, so the intended customization point lives in a file every consumer shares.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it always POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with a hardcoded `URLSearchParams` body containing only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` (see the inline comment “Customize the payload…”). adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-95) now performs an unconditional network refresh plus credential DB write in the constructor's async flow on every service instantiation with no expiry check (previously refresh was deferred to jsforce), and it bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely — inconsistent with the pattern applied to 9 sibling services — so in sync mode the stored refresh_token is the 'refresh_token' placeholder and the direct fetch to login.salesforce.com fails on every operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs an immediate token refresh via a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then writes updated credentials to DB (`prisma.credential.update(...)`) during service setup (right after reading `credential.key`). There is no expiry/need check before doing this refresh, so it will run on every instantiation. adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce uses a fragile success check, response.statusText !== 'OK', instead of response.ok.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook upsert (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58-88) is a non-atomic check-then-act: findFirst with no orderBy followed by update/create lets concurrent webhooks create duplicate (userId, appId) credentials and update an arbitrary row when duplicates already exist; the comment claiming prisma upsert can't be used is incorrect (upsert accepts any unique-constraint where), and a transaction or unique constraint would make it atomic.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts), the code does a non-atomic read-then-write: it calls prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } }) and then conditionally prisma.credential.update(...) or prisma.credential.create(...). This pattern is race-prone under concurrent webhook deliveries: two requests can both observe no row and both attempt create, potentially producing duplicates if the DB schema does not enforce uniqueness, or causing an unhandled unique-violation error if it does. Additionally, using findFirst with no orderBy means that if duplicates already exist, an arbitrary row may be updated. The diff does not show any transaction or upsert to make this atomic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook handler (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:14-31) accepts any HTTP method — a GET with no body hits appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and throws unhandled — and symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse failures are also unhandled, so malformed or hostile input produces 500s instead of 400/401 on an unauthenticated-surface-adjacent endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google Calendar credential is corrupted by the safeParse envelope: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~96-99) returns the Zod `{ success, data, error }` envelope which is stored directly as `credential.key` instead of the parsed data, so after the first token refresh every subsequent refresh and calendar operation fails until the user manually re-auths — data loss on the default path for all Google Calendar integrations

adjudication.rationale: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full Zod safeParse result (the `{ success, data, error }` envelope) rather than the parsed `data` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, it `return refreshTokenResponse;`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff changes from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (returns parsed data) to `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists `key` directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That would store the envelope object as `credential.key`, corrupting the expected credential shape for subsequent operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The minimum token schema (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11) is a silent-pass guard: `[z.string().toString()]` produces the literal key `"[object Object]"` so the effective schema is only `{ access_token: string }`, and z.object strips unknown keys — silently discarding `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, and expiry fields, while bypassing the real provider schemas (zoom, O365, Salesforce) entirely when sync is enabled, so any garbage response with an `access_token` string validates green

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate at definition time to a literal string (likely `"[object Object]"` or similar), not a pattern for arbitrary keys, so the schema effectively only *requires* `{ access_token: string }` (and maybe an optional single weird literal key). Because `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default (no `.passthrough()`), fields like `refresh_token`, `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, etc. are not preserved in `data`. When sync is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses this weakened schema instead of the provider schema, so essentially any response containing an `access_token` string can validate successfully, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricated `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` literal string overwrites the user's real refresh token: parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-29 injects the literal when parsed data lacks `refresh_token` and callers persist it — the O365 merge (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~252-254) spreads the fabricated value last over stored credentials, permanently destroying the real refresh token so the credential can never be refreshed again

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, when the parsed token data lacks `refresh_token`, mutates the parsed result by setting `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-29). In Office365 refresh, the returned parsed data is merged over existing credentials: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). If credential sharing mode is enabled (minimum schema used, which does not require/expect `refresh_token`), this will inject the literal and then overwrite the real stored `refresh_token` during the prisma update, permanently corrupting the credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sync mode returns a raw `fetch` Response where callers expect a provider-shaped token object (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16): Google's `res?.data` throws TypeError since Response has no `.data`, Hubspot reads `refresh_token`/`expires_in` off the Response and persists `undefined`/`NaN` into the credential, and Zoho's `tokenInfo.data.error` throws TypeError — every adapter breaks the moment the sync path is taken

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when sync mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), but multiple callers still treat the return value as a provider/axios-like token payload. Examples in the diff: GoogleCalendarService assigns `const token = res?.data;` after `res` comes from `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, which in sync mode is a `Response` without `.data` (will throw/produce undefined). Hubspot assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then uses token fields, which will be missing on a `Response`. Zoho Bigin does `tokenInfo.data.error` after `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, which will also fail for a `Response`. The sync path therefore breaks adapters as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The outbound token sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication at all (no secret, signature, or credential) despite the endpoint handing back live OAuth access tokens for a caller-supplied `calcomUserId`, and userIds are small sequential integers trivially enumerable — anyone who can reach the endpoint can steal access tokens for arbitrary users

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Cal.com POSTs to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no authentication material (no secret header, signature, etc.). That part of the finding is directly supported by the diff. However, the claim that “anyone who can reach the endpoint can steal access tokens” depends on how the *external* endpoint is implemented and exposed, which is not shown here. The diff does introduce an unauthenticated call pattern that is a concrete security/architecture concern for this feature, but the full exploitability is not verifiable from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` (the credential row id) as `calcomUserId` instead of `credential.userId` like every other adapter (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:~85-91), so the parent app resolves a different or nonexistent user and can silently sync another user's OAuth tokens into this credential (cross-user credential contamination)

In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call is `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`, whereas other adapters in the diff pass `credential.userId`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook find-then-act race creates duplicate credentials: `findFirst` → `update`/`create` in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:~55-89 has no transaction and no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so concurrent deliveries or a delivery racing the app's OAuth callback creates two credentials for the same user+app (duplicate events), and subsequent `findFirst` without `orderBy` updates an arbitrary row

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, credentials are written using a non-atomic find-then-act sequence: `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` followed by either `update` or `create`. There is no transaction, lock, or `upsert`/unique-key-based write, so concurrent webhook deliveries (or a race with other code creating the same credential) can lead to two `create` calls both seeing “no row” and inserting duplicates, or (if a unique constraint exists elsewhere) a thrown unique-violation error that isn’t handled. Additionally, `findFirst` has no `orderBy`, so if duplicates exist, which row gets updated is arbitrary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce now performs a full token refresh plus `prisma.credential.update` inline on every service construction (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~75-99) where jsforce previously refreshed lazily, so any transient refresh failure hard-fails the entire service; also `response.statusText !== "OK"` is fragile (HTTP/2 responses carry an empty statusText) and discards the error body, turning real failures into a meaningless 400

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new refresh logic runs immediately (fetching `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)`) before returning the `jsforce.Connection`, so any transient refresh failure will now prevent constructing/using the service at all. Additionally, the error check `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is fragile and can misclassify responses (e.g., `statusText` may be empty depending on runtime/HTTP version); it also throws a generic `HttpError` with statusCode 400 and discards the response body, losing the actual failure details.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sync fetch (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-16) has no timeout and no `response.ok` check: a slow or hung parent endpoint stalls booking-flow requests indefinitely, and a non-200 response (e.g., an HTML error page) is passed downstream to be parsed as a token response instead of failing fast

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the new sync-path uses `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and immediately returns the `response` without (a) any timeout/abort handling and (b) any `response.ok` / status validation. The diff also shows multiple call sites expecting a successful token refresh response; without fast-fail on non-2xx, downstream code will attempt to handle/parse error responses instead of failing early, and a slow/hung parent endpoint can block the awaiting request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook handler (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:27, 59-63) has no method guard and unhandled throws: `schema.parse(req.body)` throws ZodError, and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` failures turn a GET or undecryptable `keys` blob into a raw 500 instead of a 4xx, exposing zod internals and making the endpoint noisy to probe

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` handler there is no HTTP method guard (it will run for GET/PUT/etc.), and it uses throwing operations without a try/catch: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` will throw on missing/invalid body (e.g., GET where `req.body` is empty), and `symmetricDecrypt(...)` + `JSON.parse(...)` can also throw on an undecryptable/non-JSON `keys` blob or missing/invalid `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (it falls back to `""`). However, the claim that "every webhook decryption will fail" can’t be verified from the diff because `symmetricDecrypt`’s key-length requirements aren’t shown here.
